subject.title: tools.deny not enforced for claude-cli backend MCP — agents can call denied MCP tools

question: Which Claude CLI MCP enforcement boundary should OpenClaw own for `tools.deny`: generated config filtering, Claude `--disallowedTools` forwarding, a managed MCP policy proxy, or another fail-closed handoff?
rationale: The current behavior is a real security-boundary gap, but prior repair work showed that a plausible fix can widen exact MCP allow entries; maintainers need to settle the enforcement semantics before automation safely writes another fix.

options.title: Managed pre-handoff policy enforcement
options.body: Filter or proxy OpenClaw-managed MCP tools before Claude sees them, preserving exact/wildcard deny-wins behavior and adding live generated-config proof.

options.title: Claude-native deny forwarding
options.body: Map OpenClaw MCP deny entries to Claude `--disallowedTools` where possible, accepting a Claude-specific path with narrower implementation scope.

options.title: Document unsupported restrictions
options.body: Clarify CLI backend limitations and keep runtime behavior permissive, leaving operators to avoid `claude-cli` for restricted MCP deployments.

recommendation.title: Managed pre-handoff policy enforcement
recommendation.body: Filter or proxy OpenClaw-managed MCP tools before Claude sees them, preserving exact/wildcard deny-wins behavior and adding live generated-config proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The Claude CLI loopback MCP bridge and shared bundle MCP config path have the strongest feature-history signal under this handle.
